comment: Jurisdiction code profiles seeded at boot (codeProfiles.seedReferenceCodeProfiles). NEVER overwrites rows that already exist in the DB — operator edits and verifications always win. 'verified' here is reserved for values lifted verbatim from the previously hardcoded, production-proven rule constants (Oregon). Everything else ships 'seeded' and MUST be verified against official sources (research flow + human verify) before its citations are treated as authoritative.

adoptedCodes.title: Building Energy Efficiency Standards (Title 24 Part 6) — solar + storage mandate for most new construction

amendments.summary: Fire access: two 36-inch pathways on separate roof planes (one on the street/driveway side); ridge setback 18 in. when the array covers ≤33% of plan-view roof area, 36 in. when >33%.

Interconnection under CPUC Rule 21; new PG&E/SCE/SDG&E applications land on the NEM 3.0 net-billing tariff (export credits at avoided cost, ~75% below NEM 2.0). System-size expansion >10% can forfeit legacy NEM 2.0 status.
Many CA AHJs accept SolarAPP+ instant permitting for code-standard rooftop PV; structural PE stamp commonly required over ~10 kW.

fireSetbacks.description: CRC R324.6.2: 18 in. ridge setback (array ≤33% of roof plan area) / 36 in. (>33%); two 36 in. pathways on separate planes, one street-side.

amendments.summary: High-Velocity Hurricane Zone (Miami-Dade 175 mph, Broward 170 mph): every module, racking, and attachment component needs a Miami-Dade NOA (Notice of Acceptance) or Florida Product Approval with TAS impact/uplift testing; Exposure C mandatory. Engineered path is the norm — expect no prescriptive rooftop-PV track in HVHZ.
Wind uplift calcs per ASCE 7-22 component-and-cladding; attachment schedules and product approval numbers must appear on the plan set.

amendments.summary: New York AHJs generally require a PE or RA stamp on solar permit drawings, plus a structural letter whenever the array adds more than ~5 psf to the roof. Upstate snow loads (Albany 40–55 psf, Syracuse 55–70 psf, NYC ~30 psf) must carry sealed calcs.
Utility interconnection under the NY Standardized Interconnection Requirements (SIR); residential ≤25 kW is the expedited track, larger systems can trigger a CESIR study.

adoptedCodes.title: International Residential Code as commonly adopted by AZ jurisdictions
adoptedCodes.notes: SEEDED — codes are per-AHJ (Phoenix/Maricopa on newer cycles); confirm locally.

amendments.summary: As of Jan 1, 2026 every AZ municipality/county must offer instant solar permitting; Phoenix, Tucson/Pima, Maricopa, Mesa accept SolarAPP+ (eligibility: ≤25 kW AC, wood-frame roof, UL 1741 inverter, pre-approved racking, load-side interconnection, no ESS on the same permit). PE stamp typically required over ~15 kW.

adoptedCodes.title: National Electrical Code — statewide baseline for electrical licensing; most TX cities enforce NEC 2020
adoptedCodes.notes: SEEDED — building codes and solar permitting are entirely per-city; no statewide streamlining law.

amendments.summary: All TX TDSPs require IEEE 1547-2018-compliant smart inverters for interconnection; per-utility (Oncor/CenterPoint/AEP/TNMP) application processes apply outside muni/co-op territory.

adoptedCodes.title: Illinois Energy Conservation Code (statewide) — the only statewide construction code; building/electrical codes are per-jurisdiction
adoptedCodes.notes: SEEDED — Illinois has NO statewide building or electrical code; confirm each AHJ's adopted IRC/NEC cycle (many collar-county suburbs run 2018-2021 I-codes).

amendments.summary: Utility interconnection under 83 Ill. Adm. Code Part 466 (tiered review; small residential systems take the expedited track). A separate ComEd/Ameren interconnection application after permit approval is required before the system may export.

Systems interconnected on/after Jan 1, 2025 get supply-only netting (credits offset supply+transmission, not delivery) — full-retail net metering ended for new ComEd/Ameren customers. ComEd pairs this with a one-time smart-inverter rebate (~$300/kW residential; smart inverter required). ComEd NEM eligibility ≤2,000 kW AC.

Illinois Shines (Adjustable Block Program) buys 15 years of SRECs; the installer must be an IPA-registered Approved Vendor/Designee, and Distributed Generation installer certification via the ICC applies.

adoptedCodes.notes: SEEDED — confirm the current Chicago Construction Codes cycle with DOB.

adoptedCodes.title: Chicago Electrical Code (based on the 2017 NEC, with Chicago amendments — e.g. conduit requirements)
adoptedCodes.notes: SEEDED — Chicago runs its own electrical code on an older NEC basis than most of the country; plan sets citing NEC 2020/2023 articles get corrected. EMT/rigid conduit generally required where other AHJs allow cable.

amendments.summary: Structural documentation must be certified by an Illinois-licensed structural engineer or architect (all sizes). DOB permit first, then a separate ComEd interconnection application before export.

adoptedCodes.notes: SEEDED — the 2021 I-codes replaced the 2018 cycle on 1/1/2026; a plan set on the 2018 cycle may be corrected. Confirm with the municipality or its third-party agency.

adoptedCodes.notes: SEEDED — PA runs NEC 2020, NOT 2023/2026. Plan sets citing newer NEC articles get corrected.

adoptedCodes.title: ASCE 7-16 loads as referenced by the 2021 IRC/IBC

amendments.summary: BOTH a building permit and an electrical permit are required for residential rooftop PV (Philadelphia's EZ Permit is the exception: 1-2 family dwellings at or below 10 kW need only the electrical permit). Plan on a separate-permit (not combo) submittal.

Over 90% of PA's 2,562 municipalities enforce the UCC locally — via municipal staff OR a certified third-party agency (TPA), so the plan reviewer is often a private firm rather than the township. In opt-out municipalities L&I covers commercial and the owner hires a certified TPA for residential inspection. ALWAYS confirm who reviews and where the application goes before staging.

Interconnection under PUC 52 Pa. Code §75.21; AEPS mandates net metering for residential systems up to 50 kW with retail-rate credit for exports. File with the territory utility: PECO, PPL, FirstEnergy (Penelec / Met-Ed / West Penn Power / Penn Power), or Duquesne Light.
Solar contractors must hold PA Home Improvement Contractor (HIC) registration; electrical work is licensed at the municipal level (no statewide electrical license).
